questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that Utrecht has a big hospital for companion animals, and that the veterinary school in Utrecht is very well recommended internationally.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The administration part of my exchange was not the best, for my first 4-6 weeks (out of 12 weeks) I was “rejected” every Monday morning when I showed up in the department/service my schedule said. They were not expecting any students, or did not have room for me, and I was therefore told to find another place to be by myself. I did not feel like the administration did much to help me to get to know any of the local students by always sending me to departments where I was the only student (without any local student). Besides that, I was only together with the same group of local students for one day, and the next they were all new, so I did not really get the chance to make a deeper connection with any local students through school. Although most of the students and vets/educators were very kind to me and did not have a problem of switching to English even though I was the only non-Dutch speaking person in the room.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I got a contact person who was very kind and answered all my questions. I got my full schedule for the three months of exchange prior to my arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was told to be at the hospital at a certain time and call my contact person within the hospital when I got there, but unfortunately, she was on vacation during my first week, so she was not there. The reception did not really know what to with me, but after some confusion a person came to pick me up and gave me a short tour around the hospital and showed me where I should be the first week (the department I was supposed to be in the first week did not expect to have any students that week, and especially not an exchange student, but they were very adaptable and kind to me even though they were not prepared for my arrival). The administration helped me a little to find new departments to be in for the first 4-6 weeks, when the department I was supposed to be in “rejected” me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: VERY difficult! Even the local students have difficulties finding housing. Start early and do not be picky, go on facebook pages, renting websites etc. There are a few housing possibilities available through the university, but you have to be really lucky to get one of them, plus you can only rent them for a semester, and I only stayed for three months.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked being closer to the city, but miss being closer to all the other students. Most student parties, sports and social activities takes places on campus, so I would have preferred to stay on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All my course registration went through the exchange program and my contact person. My contact person asked me if I had any specific wishes for my exchange and sent my schedule for the three months exchange prior to my arrival in Utrecht.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got a contact person who helped me a lot, she answered all my questions regarding registration and all the practicalities and sent my schedule prior to my arrival in Utrecht.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the weeks I wished for and my wishes regarding being at the companion animal hospital were listened to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use your contact person, she/he can help you with most of your questions and wishes regarding your exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was more or less the same as it is in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was much alike the style of teaching in Copenhagen, you are in small groups of students who do the anamnesis and the general clinical examination, and afterwards the students discuss their findings and the treatment plan with the responsible veterinarian.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was only there for three months (not a full semester), and I had 12 weeks of clinical rotations at the companion animal hospital.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had a very kind and helpful vet in neurology, but most of the vets and departments are very kind and really experienced and at the top of their league within their field, so just go for whatever you like and are interested in.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You need to bring cash, most supermarkets (and other places) do not accept visa cards (at least not Danish visa cards).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices are more or less as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a big sports facility.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, food, social, and creativity clubs, there were a lot of opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a sports club, they have a big sports facility called “Olympus sportscentrum” where you can join most sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go visit Amsterdam, watch a football match either Ajax or Utrecht's local football team, walk along the canals in Utrecht city and visit some of the parks around Utrecht.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not a problem, the Dutch culture are much alike the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open minded and say “yes” to everything in the beginning, it might be exhausting, but it is worth it in the end. The Dutch people are (much like the danish people) a little closed/private, so in most cases you must be a bit extrovert and go look for friends yourself.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really, besides the Dutch people being a little difficult to get to know, so you have to invest some time and energy.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone speaks English.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring cash (most supermarkets do not accept card), bring a rain clothing (it rains A LOT), I would recommend to rent a bike (swapfiets) down there to get around, and if you need anything you can get it down there (there is a big shopping mall in the center of the city).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend renting a bike (Swapfiets) down there to get around.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting taught by some of the best vets in the world, they are very experienced and helpful.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administration in the beginning, that I was “rejected” every Monday morning at the department I was supposed to be in for 4-6 weeks and having to find another department/service to be in by myself. It made me feel quite unwelcome and alone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
